accuracy.evidence: Every number was checked against NASA pages: Earth to Mars about 55 to 400 million km, so at 300,000 km/s the one-way radio delay is 55e6/3e5/60 = 3.1 minutes and 400e6/3e5/60 = 22.2 minutes, shown as about 3 and about 22; trip about 7 months; Mars average about -60 C with thin carbon dioxide air; Perseverance top speed about 152 m an hour; Sojourner 1997, Curiosity in Gale Crater 2012 (rounded stream pebbles, Yellowknife Bay mudstone, mineral veins), Perseverance in Jezero Crater 2021 sealing cores in tubes. The future return is worded as 'could be brought to Earth one day', since Mars Sample Return is not yet funded.

misconceptions.evidence: The predictions and robot target the documented mistakes for this age: rovers are driven live like a remote-control car (scene 3 and robot 1), radio is instant (scene 2 prediction), Mars has flowing rivers today or never had water (scene 5 prediction, robot 3, challenge tag 'today'), and people are banned from Mars (scene 1 prediction, robot 5). The adult text names the joystick and rivers mistakes and corrects them, including the rover's own hazard cameras.

lab_distinct.evidence: The lab is built on what is special about robot explorers: a radio message timed against a draggable Earth-Mars distance, a crater grid where the learner must plan every square before one Send because live steering is impossible, tool hotspots on a rover drawing, and Mars rocks judged as water evidence. None of this works for another topic by relabelling. Gate: under 30% shingle overlap with every flagship lab, including flagastro and flagsolscale.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner discovers each idea before the text states it: opening the four panels shows that every Mars problem for a person is no problem for a machine; sending at 55 and at 400 million km shows the delay grows to about 22 minutes; sending a half-finished path makes the rover stop and wait, so the need to plan a whole route is felt; tapping a sharp rock or dune for water gets a reason, so the three water clues are learned by contrast. The done messages only confirm.

predictions.evidence: Four predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the lab then disproves: 'people are not allowed' (the panels show the real reasons), 'the message arrives at the same moment' (the timed pulse takes minutes), 'they steer it as it goes' (the plan-then-send drive), and 'Mars was always dry' (pebbles, mud layers and veins). The reveal line names the right answer after each task.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Seven challenge questions, each wrong option tagged by its slip, with six distinct feedback messages: people (names air, -60 C and 7 months), delay (separates minutes for radio from months for a rocket), live (no live steering, no people on Mars), tool (each tool's one job), water (which rocks need water and which do not) and today (dry now, wet long ago). Wrong taps inside the scenes also name the slip, e.g. a crater square says the rover could tip over, a non-adjacent square says one square at a time.

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs use short sentences and everyday words (robot on wheels, far away, too thin to breathe, like a toy car) and pass the family kid limit in validate_lessons.py. On-canvas words stay short: panel names Air, Warmth, Trip, Danger, and sayings under 12 words. Key words (rover, engineer, delay, sample, evidence) are listed in the adult text for the grown-up.

no_filler.evidence: Each kid paragraph carries one idea: what a rover is, why people have not gone, the radio delay and planning, and the tools and water evidence. The adult text gives key words, the NASA facts with numbers, the named mistakes, and what the lab asks. The content gate found no filler phrases and under 12% overlap with every other lesson.

mobile.evidence: Checked iPhone 13 dark and 360 px Android light screenshots part-way through each Show me: the four Mars panels sit in one row with 14 px labels, the detail cards wrap without clipping, the Earth label moved above Earth so it no longer overlaps the Mars label at 55 million km, the 6 x 5 crater grid fills the width with squares over 50 px, tool keys wrap to 3 + 2 on phones, and rock tiles are 2 per row. Send and Send plan keys are over 44 px tall.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button twin: the four panels ('Open the Air panel'), Nearer, Further and Send, Up, Down, Left, Right, Undo and Send plan for the drive, each tool ('Use the Drill on the arm'), each rock ('Pick: Round pebbles'), and Right or Slip. Every result is spoken through c.say and the canvas aria-label, challenge feedback is in a polite live region, and right or wrong is stated in words as well as colour. The walk gate's axe run was clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13.
